selection: First occurrence of each paired direction outcome in the frozen evaluation order. These are purposeful diagnostic cases, not a random sample or a prevalence estimate.
scope: Checked claims against the supplied prompt, not independently sourced market data. No aggregate causal claim about fine-tuning quality.

cases.label: up by 0-1%
cases.finding: Both models predict down, whereas the dataset label is up 0-1%. The adapter describes the payout ratio as high, although the supplied value is 0.1495, and calls liquidity good without a benchmark despite cashRatio 0.30424. These interpretations need support; fluent three-part structure does not verify them.

cases.label: up by 3-4%
cases.finding: Both models predict up, but neither matches the label range up 3-4% (base up 1-3%, adapter up 1-2%). The base associates healthcare partnerships with Amgen, while the supplied partnership headline concerns Nvidia. The adapter avoids that attribution, but its low-cash-ratio interpretation remains unsupported by a stated benchmark.

cases.label: up by more than 5%
cases.finding: The adapter changes the base down prediction to up, matching direction. Its up 0-1% still misses the label up more than 5%. A direction match must not be described as an accurate return magnitude. The sale and Buffett portfolio references are present in the input.

cases.label: down by 4-5%
cases.finding: The base down prediction matches direction; the adapter switches to up although the label is down 4-5%. The adapter says the AI app was upgraded by Morgan Stanley, whereas the supplied summary says Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock rating to overweight. Its high-debt claim uses longtermDebtTotalAsset 0.0926 without a stated benchmark; the new-product claim is supported by the input headline summary.
